prize_parts.citation: For the development of targeted protein degradation, in which small molecules direct E3 ubiquitin ligases to destroy chosen proteins, through heterobifunctional PROTACs and the identification of cereblon as the target of thalidomide-type molecular glues

statement.case_for: I keep B037 as a single prize part for Crews, Deshaies and Handa. The organising idea is chemical and can be tested: a small molecule that induces proximity between a protein and an E3 ligase turns pharmacology from occupancy into catalytic, event-driven removal. The first round did not change my view that this is the idea with the widest reach among the nine shortlisted. Crews and Deshaies conceived and demonstrated the heterobifunctional degrader, and Handa's identification of cereblon explained why thalidomide-class drugs work and turned molecular glues from an accident into a design principle. Both strands rest on the same induced-proximity logic and have been reproduced by many independent laboratories, with approved glue degraders already in patients. Four of eight members, including the chair and Sparr and Chabes who each reached the trio independently, name the same three people.
statement.case_against: My doubts are the same as in round 1 but I now weigh them more precisely. Attribution: any three names leave out Sakamoto, Ciulli, Gray, Ito and Kim, and Sakamoto as co-inventor of the first PROTAC is the hardest omission to defend. Maturity: no bifunctional degrader is yet approved, so part of the vindication rests on glues that were found serendipitously. Coherence: the PROTAC and glue histories differ, and a citation joining them can look assembled to fit the three-name cap. If the committee concludes that the attribution cannot be defended without Sakamoto and Ciulli, or that the clinical gap makes the timing early, Buchwald and Hartwig (B005) is the better prize: a mature, cleanly attributed two-person credit with decades of industrial use.

responses.point: Treats the cereblon glue mechanism as a separate and decisive discovery and notes that PROTACs and glues might be better recognised as two achievements.
responses.response: I considered splitting seriously, since I also see different histories. But two parts would force a cut inside the three-person limit, for instance Crews and Deshaies for PROTACs and Handa alone for cereblon, which gives the same three names while advertising the seam. Keeping one part and writing the citation around induced proximity to an E3 ligase says what the common achievement is, and it is honest that cereblon explains the glues. I agree with you that the cereblon finding is the most decisive single step on the glue side, and my citation now names it explicitly. I do not agree that the difference in history makes the prize incoherent. Lenalidomide worked before its target was known, and that is exactly why identifying the target is a discovery in its own right.

responses.point: Frames the PROTAC concept and cereblon mechanism as one idea and acknowledges that the PROTAC and glue strands arose from different groups and logic, so a trio risks looking assembled.
responses.response: I share the worry that a trio can look assembled, and I do not think it can be fully dispelled. What helps, in my view, is that the citation names a mechanism rather than a list of people: small molecules direct an E3 ligase to chosen proteins. Under that wording Crews and Deshaies (design), and Handa (mechanism of the thalidomide-type recruiters) each correspond to a part of the sentence. I also accept your point from my round-1 reply that base editing is crowded by the 2020 CRISPR prize, so I keep B060 only as a second alternative, behind B005.

responses.point: Prefers B037 for the trio but admits that his first-place ranking may reflect an appealing story, and that B016 and B005 are more mature with cleaner attribution.
responses.response: I agree that opening support is not scientific judgment, and I would not count our four votes as evidence by themselves. That is why I tested B037 against B005 on the one criterion where B005 clearly wins, attribution. My conclusion is that the clean credit of B005 does not outweigh the larger shift in how drugs are conceived. I also differ from you slightly on the clinical argument: the approved glues give the concept real clinical validation, so the missing PROTAC approval is a lag in one branch and not an absence of proof for the idea. I would revisit that if the committee thinks the trio cannot be defended.

responses.point: Prefers B005 and puts maturity ahead of conceptual novelty, treating Kosugi and Migita as acknowledged precursors and the ligand work as the decisive step.
responses.response: On the substance of B005 I agree with you more than I did in round 1. As an organic chemist I accept that the decisive step was Buchwald's and Hartwig's ligand and mechanistic work and that Kosugi and Migita are acknowledged precursors, not co-discoverers, so the precursor problem is smaller than it first looks. Where we still differ is the 2010 comparison. C-N coupling is the most important application of the palladium cross-coupling logic and I find it deserving, but a committee that has already honoured that logic will find it harder to describe as a new chemical idea. I would put maturity first only if B037 fails on attribution, which is why B005 remains my first alternative.

responses.point: Holds B005 as the overdue, well-attributed choice while conceding that B037 may be the more transformative.
responses.response: Your concession that B037 may be more transformative is what the choice comes down to. We both agree that B005 is safe on credit and maturity, and I do not call it a weak option. If the committee asks me whether a safe two-name prize or a transformative but harder-to-credit trio is the better use of this year's award, I think the second, provided the trio is defensible. I would move to B005 if the discussion shows that Sakamoto or Ciulli cannot be left out.

uncertainties: Whether the committee accepts leaving out Sakamoto and Ciulli, or whether the three-name cap makes B037 indefensible on attribution.
Whether the absence of an approved bifunctional degrader makes the timing early, given that glue degraders are already established medicines.
Whether the citation should be framed around induced proximity as a single achievement, or around PROTACs and molecular glues as separate strands.
Whether C-N coupling is distinct enough from the 2010 prize for B005 to stand as the fallback.
statement.conflict_note: No change. I have no recorded personal, institutional or collaborative tie to any credited name on the shortlist. I am a Lund colleague of Linke and Sparr, who also support B037, and I am aware that this could look like correlated judgement; our views were formed separately from our different fields. My Masamune-school training in stereocontrolled synthesis gives me no tie to any shortlisted ballot.
